g.title: LyonRank3Convo2 begins.
g.text: LyonRank3Convo2 begins.

g.title: j1185117268
g.text: If I may, I wish to tell you a story of a stray alley cat who used to come by the back of the church.

g.title: j2865151818
g.text: Go on.

g.title: j4104302508
g.text: Why?

g.title: j3426972941
g.text: [Ignore.]

g.title: j3150568527
g.text: Thank you.

g.title: j3732133698
g.text: I fear it would take more effort to explain than it would be worth.

g.title: Chat ends.
g.text: Chat ends.

g.title: j133770859
g.text: Though I suspect that this tale is not unique to this scruffy old tom, and my interactions with him seemingly noteworthy, it bears telling all the same.

g.title: j3935677924
g.text: Never mind.

g.title: j909324121
g.text: Every day he would come by to beg scraps and whatever meagre affections he could have from me or the other brothers and sisters who doted upon him.

g.title: j1970721374
g.text: He was a ragged thing, with a limp in his leg and missing part of an ear.

g.title: j1664823987
g.text: When he did not come by for a few days, Marie was quite beside herself with worry. But what is one to do for an old alley tom who has met their end, save to issue up a prayer to Lua?

g.title: j3437213928
g.text: Boolean LyonStray is now true.

g.title: j3127067167
g.text: [Let him continue.]

g.title: j3073262707
g.text: Is that allowed in your religion? Praying for animals, I mean.

g.title: j419094516
g.text: You would pray for the soul of a departed alley cat?

g.title: j2374246492
g.text: Regardless, imagine my surprise when I was fetching bread from the market and I saw the old tom sitting next to the owner of the stand.

g.title: j2687220498
g.text: +10 Chemistry

g.title: j928876576
g.text: Of course. Some of the purest, brightest souls I have encountered were encased in the flesh of a beast. It is not for me to judge how the Luminaries have set them upon their paths.

g.title: j2729301513
g.text: He greeted me with a raspy meow, as he always did, and hopped down to rub against my leg.

g.title: j3958512162
g.text: A good question. In some sects, no. It would be seen as heresy. But in ours, yes. We recognize that animals have souls.

g.title: j1462008974
g.text: Saint Elizabeth the Wise was known for her charity toward animals, though many traditions to do not recognize the Saints as apostles of the Luminaries.

g.title: j614594485
g.text: And I would note, Drifter, that he did so without a limp.

g.title: j2598847732
g.text: I find myself wondering if any influence of our order survived this long... but it was hardly the point of the conversation.

g.title: j70856091
g.text: "Ah, one of Old Devereaux's fools, I see." The man laughed as he bagged up my bread.

g.title: j1048712370
g.text: Boolean LyonLecture1 is now true.

g.title: j1662004688
g.text: It turns out the old cat was playing us, and several others, in the neighborhood. He was not starving, of failing health, or neglected in any way.

g.title: j4044921134
g.text: Indeed, if the man's words were to be believed, he was quite a murderous fiend in regards to the local population of birds.

g.title: j4204599228
g.text: Did you stop feeding Old Devereaux when he came around?

g.title: j3979550009
g.text: Are you trying to warn me about Roathe?

g.title: j670281304
g.text: Are you the alley cat in this story?

g.title: j1012991985
g.text: +10 Chemistry

g.title: j1983102731
g.text: There are a great many things to warn you about the devil "Cardinal Dimanche" put upon our doorstep. Perhaps this is one of them. Perhaps it is not.

g.title: j1859073496
g.text: The Luminaries know I have certainly been worn at the edges as of late. But is this meant to stand as a warning about myself? Perhaps. Perhaps it is not.

g.title: j1149487082
g.text: No, we did not. In fact, Marie greeted him with all the more affection for it, teasing him for being "her little imp."

g.title: j1493663410
g.text: It is simply a story to say that sometimes, when a creature seems to be in need -

g.title: j2434333902
g.text: But we no longer fretted over him. We knew that Old Devereaux could quite adequately care for himself. He did not need us.

g.title: j2421616447
g.text: +15 Chemistry

g.title: j535878670
g.text: What happened to Old Devereaux, do you know?

g.title: j350989924
g.text: What do you think drove Old Devereaux to visit you, if it wasn't need?

g.title: j1336326654
g.text: - check to see how sharp its claws may be.

g.title: j2555952630
g.text: His next disappearance, two years later, turned permanent.

g.title: j3104905189
g.text: The cynical answer I would supply you with would be "greed." For if one could have one feast, why not two? Why not ten?

g.title: j1961802150
g.text: Did you pray for him?

g.title: j2767263663
g.text: I hope he left this world comfortable and loved.

g.title: j2746535011
g.text: What would be the non-cynical answer?

g.title: j1921732882
g.text: Does that remain the same if he was only seeking affection?

g.title: j3313989738
g.text: I lit a candle for him the night I learned of his death and prayed to Lua to guide his soul to... wherever she would guide a little imp like him.

g.title: j3091392009
g.text: May I ask why?

g.title: j150504645
g.text: +10 Chemistry

g.title: j1380723803
g.text: An avaricious desire for affection is still gluttony, though it is not a hunger fed by meat and wine. And to seek it in such false pretenses?

g.title: j1188447860
g.text: And thanked Old Devereaux for all the joy he brought Marie in exchange for all those coveted bits of chicken gristle and head scratches.

g.title: j3813959388
g.text: He was an animal. He was just searching for fulfillment - food, shelter, love - he wasn't inspired by the same motivations as people. He wasn't "lying," he was hunting with a different set of tools.

g.title: j1699151276
g.text: I have seen a lot of violence, Lyon. A lot of it I have caused. I have come to hope that everyone, no matter who they are or what they've done, can have a peaceful death surrounded by those who love them.

g.title: j3785477759
g.text: I found myself oddly... respecting the cat, for the place it had found itself in the world.

g.title: j4134522493
g.text: He was a cat, Lyon. He hardly knew what he was doing.

g.title: j3380549571
g.text: We are still speaking about a cat, yes?

g.title: j157673442
g.text: Thank you. I will not hinder you in your day any longer.

g.title: j1414826405
g.text: He wasn't denying others anything by making you all his "fools." If anything... you all seem to have been enriched by his visits.

g.title: j828390386
g.text: Fascinating. I would expect you to despise your enemies. But that is my own folly - to assume I know how anyone in this day and age would comport themselves.

g.title: j382433235
g.text: Here was a creature who had learned to use its condition - its appearance, its age, its scars - as a weapon against "the fools" around him who did not see through his ruse.

g.title: j1930645756
g.text: He knew well enough to feign a limp.

g.title: j2485813266
g.text: Infer from this conversation whatever you wish, Drifter.

g.title: j944546954
g.text: -F. Lyon Allard

g.title: j4142512107
g.text: Add -1 to Thermostat counter

g.title: j984915553
g.text: Add 1 to Thermostat counter

g.title: j382264891
g.text: An imp in matted fur, he truly was. Yet I found myself petting him all the same when he came 'round to visit.

g.title: j3853206177
g.text: Yes. I suppose we were. And we were not experiencing a shortage of bits of chicken gristle and scratches.

g.title: j507060350
g.text: Let alone someone with your particularly fascinating upbringing.

g.title: j2153812812
g.text: And equally heartbroken when, two years later, his next disappearance was permanent.

g.title: j1162557709
g.text: Perhaps that is why I lit a candle for him and prayed to Lua to take his soul and guide it to... wherever she would take a little imp like him.

g.title: j1251440446
g.text: +5 Chemistry

g.title: j742294221
g.text: +5 Chemistry

g.title: j2306704805
g.text: Thank you. I will not hinder you in your day any longer. This has been a most interesting conversation. Until we speak again.

g.title: j2620086161
g.text: And why I thanked Old Devereaux in my prayers that night for all the joy he had brought Marie.

g.title: j95436330
g.text: Perhaps his little villainy was of some good in a roundabout manner.
